job_location: Camperdown, Royal Prince Alfred Hospital | Sydney
responsibilities: The Senior Analytics Engineer is the technical lead responsible for the design, build, and optimisation of the organisation's new cloud data platform — pipelines, data models, and reporting layer components — built from the ground up, retrieving relevant business logic from the legacy SQL environment and archiving selected legacy databases to the cloud where required, to deliver trusted, actionable insight that meets the organisation's clinical and operational needs.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: to deliver trusted, actionable insight that meets the organisation's clinical and operational needs
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Trust, production-grade platforms, monitoring and failover carry the posting; there is no speed or shipping language at all.
evidence.domain_risk: Join the Performance Unit at one of Australia's leading public health organisations
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: A public health district where the reporting layer serves clinical needs, so errors reach patient-facing operational decisions.
evidence.collaboration_width: No distinctly named partner teams — only the role holder's own Performance Unit.
evidence.data_team_maturity: the organisation's new cloud data platform — pipelines, data models, and reporting layer components — built from the ground up
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The platform is being built "from the ground up" while business logic still lives in a legacy SQL environment.
evidence.jd_authorship: retrieving relevant business logic from the legacy SQL environment and archiving selected legacy databases to the cloud where required
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The role summary names the actual migration problem and the requirements name Snowflake, dbt Core, monitoring and failover.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: pipelines, data models, and reporting layer components
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The deliverable is the platform and reporting layer itself, serving the organisation's downstream consumers rather than one business function.
evidence.autonomy_level: is the technical lead responsible for the design, build, and optimisation of the organisation's new cloud data platform
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Named as the technical lead who owns design and build of the whole platform.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: AI is not mentioned anywhere in the posting.
evidence.testing_framing: platform automation, and operational tooling - such as monitoring, failover, and data movement
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Monitoring appears only inside a requirements bullet about platform tooling, with no ownership of a data quality practice.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Failover and monitoring signal concern about platform outages, but the posting carries no compliance or audit framing despite the health setting.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The platform is explicitly new and built from scratch, with the legacy estate being migrated away from.
evidence.loss_aversion: "to deliver trusted, actionable insight that meets the organisation's clinical and operational needs" — trust is named as the purpose of the platform.
